subject_line: Extra butter might be why you've stalled
opening: Happy Sunday, friends. This week we got into some spicy territory: fat stalls, second-attempt keto misery, and a Reddit coffee thread that apparently broke the internet. Grab your ribeye and let's get into it.

hero.title: Can You Really Eat Too Much Fat on Keto?
hero.teaser: Most of us started keto after hearing 'fat is your friend.' So it's genuinely shocking when adding more butter to everything turns out to be the exact thing slowing you down. The difference between dietary fat and body fat is where this gets interesting, and it's not what the usual keto advice will tell you. Sarah breaks down the actual science, and the answer depends on one factor most people aren't tracking. You'll want to read this before your next grocery run.

supporting.title: Why Your Second Attempt at Keto Feels Harder
supporting.teaser: Sarah found the biological reason round two hits so much rougher, and it has nothing to do with willpower.

supporting.title: Transitioning Off the Lion Diet: A Practical Guide
supporting.teaser: Chloe maps out the reintroduction order most people get wrong, plus the two mistakes that erase your progress fast.

supporting.title: Quitting Coffee on Carnivore: The Thread That Won't Die
supporting.teaser: A 68-comment Reddit thread revealed it's not really about the coffee, and Chloe explains what it's actually about.

try_this_week: Track your added fat separately for three days. Don't change what you eat yet. Just log butter, tallow, and cream as their own line item so you can see the actual number. Most people are surprised, and that number is the first thing to look at if your scale hasn't moved in two weeks.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something the community has been asking about for months, and the answer is going to make a lot of people rethink their morning routine.
